questions.stem: A small petrol fire breaks out under a car in a workshop in Kaduna. Which extinguisher should NOT be used on it?
questions.explanation: Water spreads burning petrol because petrol floats on it; foam, dry powder or sand smother the fire.

questions.stem: Before working under a vehicle raised on a trolley jack, the mechanic must
options: leave the engine running in neutral
support the vehicle on axle stands placed at the correct points
questions.explanation: Jacks can fail or be knocked; axle stands at the jacking points give secure support.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to tighten cylinder head bolts to the manufacturer's specified value?
questions.explanation: A torque wrench measures the tightening torque; a ring spanner gives no measure of torque.

questions.stem: In a front-engine, front-wheel-drive car, the drive is taken to the front wheels through
options: a transaxle and drive shafts with constant-velocity joints
a long propeller shaft and a live rear axle
a chain from the engine to the rear wheels
questions.explanation: FWD combines gearbox and final drive in a transaxle and uses CV-jointed drive shafts; a propeller shaft and live axle belong to rear-wheel drive.

questions.stem: In a four-stroke engine, the camshaft rotates at
options: the same speed as the crankshaft
twice the speed of the crankshaft
half the speed of the crankshaft
a quarter of the speed of the crankshaft
questions.explanation: Each valve opens once every two crankshaft revolutions, so the camshaft is geared at half crankshaft speed.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly compares a diesel engine with a petrol engine of similar size?
options: The diesel uses spark plugs and a carburettor
The diesel has a lower compression ratio to avoid knocking
The diesel is lighter and quieter
The diesel uses a higher compression ratio and ignites its fuel by the heat of compression
questions.explanation: Diesel engines (about 14:1 to 22:1) rely on compression ignition; they are usually heavier and noisier than petrol engines.

questions.stem: An engine's inlet valve opens 12 degrees before TDC and closes 48 degrees after BDC. Its exhaust valve opens 50 degrees before BDC and closes 10 degrees after TDC. The valve overlap is
questions.explanation: Overlap is the period both valves are open around TDC: inlet opens 12 degrees BTDC + exhaust closes 10 degrees ATDC = 22 degrees. (The inlet is open for 240 degrees.)

questions.stem: A cylinder has a swept volume of 450 cm^3 and a clearance volume of 50 cm^3. Its compression ratio is
questions.explanation: CR = (swept + clearance) / clearance = (450 + 50) / 50 = 10 : 1; 9 : 1 forgets to add the clearance volume.

questions.stem: A common firing order for a four-cylinder in-line engine whose cylinders are numbered from the front is
questions.explanation: With crank throws 1 and 4 together and 2 and 3 together, firing 1-3-4-2 (or 1-2-4-3) spaces the power strokes evenly; 1-5-3-6-2-4 is a six-cylinder order.

questions.stem: The chemically correct (stoichiometric) air-fuel ratio for petrol is about
questions.explanation: About 14.7 kg of air burns 1 kg of petrol completely; richer or weaker mixtures depart from this.

questions.stem: In a multi-point electronic fuel injection system, petrol is injected
options: by one injector per cylinder into each inlet port
by a single injector above the throttle valve
questions.explanation: Multi-point systems have an injector for each cylinder; single-point (throttle body) systems use one injector for all cylinders.

questions.stem: Heater (glow) plugs are fitted to many indirect-injection diesel engines to
options: ignite the fuel at every power stroke
heat the combustion chamber air for easier cold starting
warm the diesel in the fuel tank
questions.explanation: Glow plugs only assist cold starting; normal combustion is by heat of compression.

questions.stem: A silencer that reduces noise by passing exhaust gas through perforated tubes surrounded by glass fibre or steel wool is the
questions.explanation: Absorption silencers soak up sound energy in packing; baffle types reflect pressure waves through chambers.

questions.stem: In the oil grade SAE 20W-50, the letter W indicates that the oil
options: is for use in two-stroke petroil mixtures
meets a viscosity requirement at low (winter) temperature
questions.explanation: W means winter: the oil behaves like SAE 20 when cold and like SAE 50 at operating temperature.

questions.stem: Lubrication of a two-stroke motorcycle engine by mixing oil with the petrol is known as
questions.explanation: In petroil systems the oil travels with the fuel through the crankcase to lubricate bearings and cylinder walls.

questions.stem: The thermostat in a water-cooled engine
options: keeps the coolant from flowing to the radiator until the engine reaches working temperature
raises the boiling point of the coolant
questions.explanation: The thermostat valve stays closed when cold so the engine warms up quickly, then opens to the radiator.

questions.stem: The main purpose of a pressure cap on the radiator is to
options: lower the boiling point of the coolant
stop the water pump from leaking
raise the boiling point of the coolant
questions.explanation: Pressurising the system raises the boiling point, so the engine can run hotter without boiling the coolant.

questions.stem: A car has a first-gear ratio of 3.2 : 1 and a final drive ratio of 4.1 : 1. When the engine turns at 2952 rev/min in first gear, the road wheels turn at
questions.explanation: Overall ratio = 3.2 x 4.1 = 13.12 : 1; wheel speed = 2952 / 13.12 = 225 rev/min. Ratios multiply, they do not add.

questions.stem: A driving gear with 14 teeth meshes with a driven gear of 42 teeth. The gear ratio is
questions.explanation: Gear ratio = driven teeth / driver teeth = 42 / 14 = 3 : 1 (speed reduction, torque increase).

questions.stem: A single-plate clutch has two friction surfaces, coefficient of friction 0.3, total spring force 4000 N and mean radius 100 mm. The torque it can transmit is
questions.explanation: T = mu x W x R x n = 0.3 x 4000 x 0.1 x 2 = 240 N m.

questions.stem: The device in the gearbox that equalises the speeds of the gear and the shaft before they lock together is the
questions.explanation: The synchroniser's cone clutch matches speeds so dog teeth engage quietly; the interlock prevents two gears being selected together.

questions.stem: A tyre is marked 195/65 R15. Taking 1 inch = 25.4 mm, the overall diameter of the inflated tyre is about
questions.explanation: Sidewall height = 195 x 0.65 = 126.75 mm; diameter = 15 x 25.4 + 2 x 126.75 = 634.5 mm.

questions.stem: One advantage of a tubeless tyre over a tubed tyre is that it
options: can be fitted to any spoked wheel
loses air slowly when punctured by a nail
is cheaper to repair on the road without tools
questions.explanation: The tyre seals around the object so air escapes slowly; spoked wheels normally need tubes.

questions.stem: In a hydraulic brake system a force of 600 N acts on a master cylinder piston of 20 mm diameter. The force on a wheel-cylinder piston of 40 mm diameter is
questions.explanation: Pressure is the same throughout; force is proportional to area, i.e. to diameter squared: 600 x (40/20)^2 = 2400 N.

questions.stem: A spongy brake pedal that can be pumped up is most likely caused by
questions.explanation: Air compresses, so the pedal feels spongy; bleeding the brakes removes it.

questions.stem: The backward tilt of the king pin (steering axis) when viewed from the side of the vehicle, which gives the steering a self-centring action, is
questions.explanation: Castor places the steering axis ahead of the tyre contact point so the wheel trails and self-centres; camber is the tilt of the wheel viewed from the front.

questions.stem: The type of steering gearbox in which a pinion on the steering column meshes with a toothed bar is
questions.explanation: In rack and pinion steering the rotating pinion moves the rack sideways to push the track rods.

questions.stem: The main function of a shock absorber (damper) is to
options: carry the weight of the vehicle
reduce the oscillation of the spring after a bump
increase tyre grip by raising pressure
questions.explanation: Springs carry the load; the damper converts the spring's oscillation energy into heat so the body stops bouncing.

questions.stem: Two lamps, each of resistance 6 ohms, are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. The total current drawn is
questions.explanation: Parallel resistance = 6/2 = 3 ohms; I = 12 / 3 = 4 A.

questions.stem: In the earth-return wiring system used on most cars, the return path for current to the battery is through
options: a second insulated cable for every circuit
questions.explanation: Using the body as the return conductor saves cable and weight; the battery negative is bonded to the body.

questions.stem: The electrolyte in a lead-acid battery is a mixture of
questions.explanation: Lead-acid batteries use dilute sulphuric acid; potassium hydroxide is the alkaline-cell electrolyte.

questions.stem: The sparking plug gap is checked and set with a
questions.explanation: Feeler or wire gauges are slid into the gap; the side electrode is bent to adjust it.

questions.stem: One advantage of an alternator over a dynamo (d.c. generator) for vehicle charging is that the alternator
options: needs a commutator to give direct current
has no need for a voltage regulator
produces alternating current that the battery can store directly
gives a useful charging output even at engine idling speed
questions.explanation: Alternators can be geared to spin fast and give output at idle; they use diodes, not a commutator, and still need a regulator.

questions.stem: A blade-type fuse coloured red in a car fuse box is normally rated at
questions.explanation: Standard blade fuse colours: tan 5 A, red 10 A, blue 15 A, yellow 20 A, green 30 A.

questions.stem: The windscreen wiper blades always stop at the bottom of the screen when switched off because of the
options: park (limit) switch in the wiper motor
questions.explanation: The park switch keeps the motor running until the blades reach the rest position.

questions.stem: An electronic component that allows current to flow in one direction only is a
questions.explanation: A diode conducts in its forward direction and blocks reverse current; this is used in rectifiers.

questions.stem: An advantage of a Hall-effect trigger over an inductive (magnetic pulse) trigger in electronic ignition is that the Hall-effect signal
options: does not depend on engine speed, so it can be checked with the engine stationary
gives a larger voltage as engine speed rises
removes the need for an ignition coil
questions.explanation: A Hall sensor switches according to the presence of the vane, giving a constant-amplitude square wave even at zero speed; an inductive pickup's output rises with speed.

questions.stem: Compared with a carburettor, electronic fuel injection gives
options: a simpler system that needs no sensors
no need for an electrical supply
more accurate mixture control, better economy and lower emissions
questions.explanation: The ECU meters fuel from sensor inputs, giving precise mixtures; it is more complex and depends on electrical power.

questions.stem: In a vehicle air-conditioning system, the component inside the passenger compartment that absorbs heat from the cabin air is the
questions.explanation: Refrigerant evaporates in the evaporator, absorbing heat; the condenser at the front of the car releases it outside.

questions.stem: According to the highway code, a triangular road sign with a red border is a
questions.explanation: Triangles warn of hazards ahead; circles give orders and rectangles give information or directions.

questions.stem:
(a) With the aid of a description, explain the operation of a four-stroke cycle petrol engine. [8 marks]
(b) The inlet valve of an engine opens 8 degrees before TDC and closes 42 degrees after BDC, while the exhaust valve opens 45 degrees before BDC and closes 12 degrees after TDC. Calculate (i) the inlet valve open period (ii) the exhaust valve open period (iii) the valve overlap. [6 marks]
(c) State the purpose of valve overlap. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Induction: piston moves down, inlet valve open, air-fuel mixture drawn in
2 marks: (a) Compression: both valves closed, piston moves up compressing the mixture
2 marks: (a) Power: spark ignites mixture near TDC, expanding gases force piston down
2 marks: (a) Exhaust: exhaust valve open, piston moves up expelling burnt gases; cycle takes two crankshaft revolutions
2 marks: (b)(i) Inlet period = 8 + 180 + 42 = 230 degrees
2 marks: (b)(ii) Exhaust period = 45 + 180 + 12 = 237 degrees
2 marks: (b)(iii) Overlap = 8 + 12 = 20 degrees
1 mark: (c) Uses gas momentum to scavenge exhaust gases and improve cylinder filling at speed
questions.explanation: Induction, compression, power and exhaust strokes over two revolutions. Inlet open 8 + 180 + 42 = 230 degrees; exhaust 45 + 180 + 12 = 237 degrees; overlap 8 + 12 = 20 degrees, which helps scavenging and filling.

questions.stem:
(a) State three functions of the clutch. [3 marks]
(b) Describe the operation of a single-plate coil-spring clutch when the pedal is depressed and released. [6 marks]
(c) A gearbox has the following teeth: constant-mesh pinion 18, layshaft constant-mesh gear 36, layshaft second gear 24, mainshaft second gear 36. Calculate the second-gear ratio. [4 marks]
(d) State two causes of clutch slip. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Any three, 1 mark each: allows smooth take-up of drive from rest; disconnects engine from gearbox for gear changing; allows engine to run while vehicle is stationary in gear; protects transmission from shock loads
3 marks: (b) Released: springs press pressure plate against driven plate and flywheel, friction locks them and drive passes to the gearbox input shaft
3 marks: (b) Depressed: release bearing pushes levers/diaphragm, pressure plate is pulled back against spring force, driven plate is freed and drive is disconnected
3 marks: (c) Ratio = (36/18) x (36/24) (2) = 2 x 1.5 (1) = 3 : 1 (1)
1 mark: (c) Statement that ratios multiply: driven/driver for each pair
2 marks: (d) Any two, 1 mark each: worn or oil-contaminated linings; weak/broken springs; no free play at pedal; warped pressure plate
questions.explanation: Clutch: smooth take-up, disconnects drive for gear changes, isolates engine when stationary. Pedal released - springs clamp driven plate between flywheel and pressure plate; depressed - release bearing withdraws pressure plate. Second gear = (36/18) x (36/24) = 3 : 1. Slip: worn/oily linings, weak springs, no free play.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the operation of a hydraulic braking system from the pedal to the wheels. [6 marks]
(b) State three advantages of disc brakes over drum brakes. [3 marks]
(c) Explain the purpose of a vacuum servo in a braking system. [2 marks]
(d) State four brake faults and one cause of each. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) Driver presses pedal (1); pushrod moves master cylinder piston (1); pressure is created in brake fluid (1); pressure transmitted equally through pipes and hoses (Pascal's principle) (1); wheel cylinder/caliper pistons move out (1); shoes/pads pressed against drums/discs, friction slows the wheel; springs/seals return them on release (1)
3 marks: (b) Any three, 1 mark each: better heat dissipation so less fade; self-cleaning, sheds water; self-adjusting; easier pad replacement; more even braking
2 marks: (c) Uses engine manifold vacuum (pressure difference) to add force to the driver's pedal effort, reducing pedal effort
4 marks: (d) Any four, 1 mark each fault with cause: spongy pedal - air in system; pulling to one side - contaminated/unevenly worn linings or seized piston; brake fade - overheating; squeal - glazed/worn pads; low pedal - worn linings or fluid leak; brakes binding - seized pistons or no pedal free play
questions.explanation: Pedal moves the master cylinder piston, pressurising fluid that acts equally on wheel cylinders or calipers, forcing linings against drums/discs. Discs dissipate heat better, shed water and self-adjust. A vacuum servo uses manifold vacuum to boost pedal force. Faults: spongy pedal (air), pulling (contaminated lining), fade (overheating), squeal (glazed pads).

questions.stem:
(a) State three methods of heat transfer and give an example of each in an engine cooling system. [6 marks]
(b) Describe the operation of a wax-pellet thermostat. [4 marks]
(c) Compare air cooling and water cooling, giving two advantages of each. [4 marks]
(d) State one reason for flushing a radiator. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) 2 marks each: conduction - heat through cylinder wall to coolant/fins; convection - circulation of coolant (thermosyphon) or air flow; radiation - heat given off from radiator/engine surfaces
4 marks: (b) Wax sealed in a copper capsule (1); when heated the wax melts and expands (1); expansion pushes the valve open against a spring, letting coolant flow to the radiator (1); on cooling the wax contracts and the spring closes the valve (1)
2 marks: (c) Air cooling, any two: lighter; no coolant leaks/freezing; fewer parts; warms up quickly
2 marks: (c) Water cooling, any two: more even temperature control; quieter; easier cabin heating; suits high-output multi-cylinder engines
1 mark: (d) To remove rust, scale and sludge that block the tubes and reduce cooling
questions.explanation: Conduction through metal, convection of coolant/air, radiation from radiator. Wax pellet expands when hot, opening the valve; spring closes it when cool. Air cooling is light and simple; water cooling is quieter with better temperature control. Flushing clears scale and rust.

questions.stem:
(a) State the function of each of the following in the starting system: (i) battery (ii) solenoid (iii) starter motor (iv) flywheel ring gear. [4 marks]
(b) Explain why the starter motor is series wound. [2 marks]
(c) Name two types of starter motor drive. [2 marks]
(d) A starter motor cranks the engine very slowly. State four possible causes. [4 marks]
(e) State three safety precautions when testing a starting system. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) 1 mark each: battery - supplies cranking current; solenoid - heavy-duty switch, also engages pinion in pre-engaged type; starter motor - converts electrical energy to mechanical torque to turn engine; ring gear - receives drive from pinion to turn crankshaft
2 marks: (b) Series motor gives very high torque at low speed/at start, needed to overcome engine compression and friction
2 marks: (c) 1 mark each: inertia (Bendix) drive; pre-engaged drive (also axial/sliding armature)
4 marks: (d) Any four, 1 mark each: low battery charge; corroded/loose terminals or earth strap; worn brushes; dirty commutator; worn bushes letting armature drag; thick oil/tight engine; undersized cables
3 marks: (e) Any three, 1 mark each: gearbox in neutral and handbrake on; disconnect ignition/fuel so engine does not start when testing; keep hands and leads clear of moving parts; avoid sparks near battery; remove watches and rings
questions.explanation: Battery supplies current, solenoid switches heavy current, motor turns the engine via pinion and ring gear. Series winding gives maximum torque at low speed. Drives: inertia and pre-engaged. Slow cranking: weak battery, bad connections, worn brushes, dirty commutator, worn bushes. Precautions: neutral, handbrake, disable ignition, keep clear, avoid sparks.

questions.stem:
(a) State three purposes of a suspension system. [3 marks]
(b) Distinguish between rigid beam axle and independent suspension, giving one advantage of each. [6 marks]
(c) Compare the semi-elliptic leaf spring with the coil spring, giving two advantages of each. [4 marks]
(d) State two symptoms of worn shock absorbers. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Any three, 1 mark each: absorb road shocks; give passenger comfort; keep tyres in contact with the road; support vehicle weight; maintain wheel alignment/stability
3 marks: (b) Rigid beam: wheels on both sides joined by one solid axle so a bump on one wheel affects the other (2); advantage - simple, strong, cheap, suits heavy loads (1)
3 marks: (b) Independent: each wheel moves up and down without affecting the other (2); advantage - better ride and road holding, lower unsprung weight (1)
2 marks: (c) Leaf spring, any two: also locates the axle; carries heavy loads; inter-leaf friction gives some damping; simple
2 marks: (c) Coil spring, any two: lighter; softer ride; compact; no lubrication needed; long life
2 marks: (d) Any two, 1 mark each: excessive bouncing after bumps; nose diving on braking; oil leaking from damper; uneven tyre wear; poor road holding
questions.explanation: Suspension absorbs shocks, gives comfort, keeps tyres on the road and supports the weight. Rigid axle links both wheels (strong, simple); independent lets each wheel move on its own (better ride). Leaf springs locate the axle and carry heavy loads; coil springs are light and compact. Worn dampers cause bouncing, nose-dive, leaks and uneven tyre wear.
